newsitem.title: UK: MOTORCYCLING-KOCINSKI TAKES SUPERBIKE CHAMPIONSHIP LEAD.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-KOCINSKI TAKES SUPERBIKE CHAMPIONSHIP LEAD.

text.p: America's John Kocinski bagged a second and a fourth place for Honda at Brands Hatch on Sunday to take the lead in the world superbike championship.
The Honda rider took full advantage of a crash in the first race by Carl Fogarty to overhaul the Briton in the standings and now leads by four points after seven rounds.
Fogarty crashed on lap five in the opener, won by Italian Pier-Francesco Chilli on a Ducati, with Kocinski finishing fourth.
Ducati team mates Fogarty and Chilli collided in the second race, forcing the Italian out, but the Briton recovered and overcame a slippery track to take the honours.
However, Kocinski's second place was good enough for the overall lead. "It's been some day but I've come out of this with the title lead and that's not something I expected," he said.

A record crowd of more than 67,000 squeezed into Brands Hatch and had the added bonus of seeing two Britons take third places - Yamaha's Niall Mackenzie in the first and Honda rider Michael Rutter in the second.
Sudden showers left the riders on a wet track on slick tyres, causing several crashes and restarts.

British rider Graeme Ritchie was airlifted to hospital after crashing on lap three of the opening race and was under intensive care on Sunday night. He was reported to be "serious but stable" with head and chest injuries.
